A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same contrastive-concept segmentation work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting, relocated material, and the new Appendix E in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original segmentation evaluations, ablations, sensitivity studies, and qualitative analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds runtime and memory measurements in Appendix E and Table 10.

M1.justification: The co-occurrence-based and LLM-based concept-generation procedures, filtering steps, nearest-neighbor mapping, and multi-query handling remain unchanged. The redesigned overview depicts the existing method; Mixtral remains the generator used for the segmentation experiments.

E1.justification: Both versions retain VOC, Context, COCO-Object, COCO-Stuff, Cityscapes, ADE20K, and the LAION-derived co-occurrence data. The added timing study reuses Pascal VOC queries rather than introducing new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix E.1 adds a brief resource-cost comparison with Llama 3 8B Instruct, Gemma-2 9B Instruct, and Gemma-3 4B, although individual measurement details are not supplied. Segmentation comparators are retained: Table 2's switch from CLIP-DINOiser to GEM redisplays comparisons already present in v2 Table 4.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces timing protocols: generation averaged over 20 Pascal VOC queries and separate text-embedding and segmentation timings, with the latter using 448×448 images and pre-extracted text embeddings. Existing segmentation evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new efficiency analysis examines concept-generation costs and separates text-encoding overhead from segmentation cost. Existing filtering ablations, parameter studies, failure cases, feature-space analyses, sigmoid experiments, WordNet filtering, and part-removal analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 10 introduces runtime uncertainty reporting, such as 49.2±0.7 ms, absent from v2. The meaning of the ± values and the number of timing repetitions are unspecified; no additional repeated segmentation evaluations are established.

E6.justification: Appendix E newly reports Mixtral's 25.5 GB memory requirement and 5.4-second generation time. Table 10 reports text-embedding times of 49.2 versus 519.5 ms and segmentation times of 22.1 versus 22.3 ms for CC_BG versus CC_D. Matched segmentation scores and existing qualitative findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The segmentation-map definitions, co-occurrence normalization, similarity filtering, and IoU-single computation are retained. Algorithm 1 is relocated without changing its computation; no new formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the single-query problem formulation, IoU-single metric, two contrastive-concept generation approaches, and claims of applicability across segmenters. The expanded title and terminology clarification do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly explains that additional text embeddings dominate runtime overhead while the segmentation forward pass changes little. It discusses caching's memory tradeoff and smaller LLM alternatives. Existing failure explanations and applicability limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds hardware information, including an A100 for LLM measurements and an Intel i7/RTX A5000 system for online extraction timings, plus processing and caching guidance. Mixtral v0.1, 4-bit precision, flash attention, and the prompts were already disclosed in v2.

R1.justification: v3 explicitly distinguishes its setup from open-set unknown-class identification using Wu et al. (2024). It adds references including CLIPSelf, MasqCLIP, the 2023 MaskCLIP work, and Llama/Gemma reports. The central positioning of automatic, query-specific contrastive concepts remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized language and terminology edits, updates the title and affiliations, and adds impact, acknowledgment, and efficiency sections. Method-overview and metric explanations move into the main text, while the principal argument and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: TMLR formatting changes typography, running headers, spacing, and figure/table placement throughout. The method overview and metric illustration are redrawn, enlarged, and moved from v2 Figures 6–7 to v3 Figures 3 and 5. Table 2 is recomposed and runtime Table 10 is added.

improvement.justification: v3 supplies previously missing practical-cost evidence, exposing substantial text-embedding overhead while showing similar segmentation times. The revised main-text diagrams and terminology also improve accessibility, with earlier results and limitations retained. Undefined runtime uncertainty and limited details for the alternative-LLM comparison temper these gains; the core accuracy evidence is unchanged.
